title: Senegal World Cup squad: Mane in, Diao returns, surprise call-up for Ndiaye, 18
content:
Senegal have named their 28-man squad for the World Cup.

Talismanic forward Sadio Mane, the country’s record scorer with 53 international goals, is the biggest name in Pape Thiaw’s 28-man selection.

The former Liverpool star, 34, who plays for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia, missed the Qatar World Cup in 2022 with a knee injury.

In January’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final Mane was crucial in persuading his team-mates to return after they left the field in protest when hosts Morocco were awarded a controversial penalty.

Senegal returned and won the game 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, though African football’s governing body CAF later declared Morocco winners.

There are seven Premier League representatives, including Chelsea’s Mamadou Sarr, midfielder Idrissa Gana Gueye and forwards Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr.

Como winger Assane Diao, 20, is back after missing AFCON with an injury amid a club-versus-country row.

Head coach Cesc Fabregas played Diao against Roma, where he picked up an injury which ruled him out of the tournament.

Fabregas, speaking to Sky Italia, had criticised Diao’s initial inclusion in the squad, while admitting the winger “probably shouldn’t have played” against Roma, but thought it was worth taking “the risk” as he would be unavailable for Como due to his AFCON commitments.

Thiaw must cut his squad by two to the FIFA-mandated 26 before June 2.

Perhaps former Paris Saint-Germain defender Abdou Diallo, who plays for Qatari side Umm-Salal.

However Sarr, 20, and Lyon’s Moussa Niakhate, competing for the left-sided centre-half role, are playing in higher quality leagues.

Rassoul Ndiaye, a regular for Le Havre in France’s Ligue 1, has tough competition in midfield but could have been included at the expense of one of the extra forwards.

Forwards Idrissa Gueye (no relation to Everton’s Gana Gueye), 19, and 20-year-old Mamadou Diakhon have impressed in patches for Udinese and Club Brugge respectively, but their time will come.

Lens winger Abdallah Sima has probably not done enough.

How about the teenage bolter Bara Sapoko Ndiaye?

The 18-year-old is uncapped for his country at senior level and is on loan from Gambian side Gambinos Stars Africa to German giants Bayern Munich.

He made his professional debut on April 11 and has since started two matches for the Bundesliga champions.

Ndiaye is a complete wildcard and is therefore a bold and exciting inclusion from Thiaw, who has shown he is willing to blood talented youngsters like Ibrahim Mbaye and Mamadou Sarr.

Versatile full-back Ilay Camara is there as cover, with Moustapha Mbow perhaps there if Thiaw opts for a back three in defence.

Target man Cherif Ndiaye has won the race to act as the backup striker.

Veteran Nampalys Mendy, 33, has played sporadically for Watford in England’s second tier and is one of the biggest names left out, with 36 caps.

There is no space for Vancouver Whitecaps winger Cheikh Sabaly.

Meanwhile, Lazio’s Boulaye Dia and Metz’s Habib Diallo are slightly more established at international level than Cherif Ndiaye, who plays for Turkish side Samsunspor, but the latter has outscored them both this season.

Senegal face Mauricio Pochettino’s U.S. men’s national team in Charlotte, North Carolina on May 31 before taking on Saudi Arabia at Toyota Field in San Antonio, Texas on June 10.

They play France on June 16 to begin their tournament — Senegal famously beat the French world champions in 2002 — before taking on Norway on June 23 and Iraq on June 26 to round off a tough-looking Group I.

They reached the quarter-finals in 2002, which remains their best ever World Cup finish, and as one of the best teams in Africa will be looking to match that achievement.

Goalkeepers: Mory Diaw (Le Havre), Yehvann Diouf (Nice), Edouard Mendy (Al-Ahli).

Defenders: Ilay Camara (Anderlecht), Krepin Diatta (Monaco), El Hadji Malick Diouf (West Ham United), Ismail Jakobs (Galatasaray), Kalidou Koulibaly (Al-Hilal), Moustapha Mbow (Paris FC), Antoine Mendy (Nice), Moussa Niakhaté (Lyon), Mamadou Sarr (Chelsea), Abdoulaye Seck (Maccabi Haifa).

Midfielders: Lamine Camara (Monaco), Pathé Ciss (Rayo Vallecano), Habib Diarra (Sunderland), Idrissa Gana Gueye (Everton), Pape Gueye (Villarreal), Bara Ndiaye (Bayern Munich), Pape Matar Sarr (Tottenham).

Forwards: Assane Diao (Como), Bamba Dieng (Lorient), Nicolas Jackson (Bayern Munich), Sadio Mané (Al-Nassr),  Ibrahim Mbaye (Paris Saint-Germain), Cherif Ndiaye (Samsunspor), Iliman Ndiaye (Everton), Ismaila Sarr (Crystal Palace).
